title: Egg Brand Henfruit Raises $15 Mn In First External Funding Round
summary: Egg brand Henfruit raises $15 million in first external funding round
detailed: Egg brand Henfruit raised $15 Mn (about ₹140 Cr) in its first external funding Series A round led by Lok Capital, DSG Consumer Partners, and RPSG Capital Ventures.
Founded in 2014 by Tarun Gupta, the company currently processes over 4 Cr eggs a month, operates in 15 cities, employs over 300 people, and expects FY27 revenue to exceed ₹350 Cr.
The new capital will be used to expand online and offline distribution across India, scale production capacity, and strengthen its supply chain.

The brand distributes its products through its website, quick commerce platforms like Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Blinkit, Milkbasket, and e-commerce platforms such as BigBasket, Amazon India, and Flipkart.
sentences: The round marks the company’s first external fundraise since Tarun Gupta founded it in 2014.
Henfruit said it will use the capital to widen its online and offline distribution across India, expand production capacity, and scale its supply chain.
The company says it processes over 4 Cr eggs a month, serves customers in 15 cities, and employs more than 300 people.
It expects revenue to exceed ₹350 Cr in FY27.
The brand sells through its website and platforms including Zepto, Swiggy Instamart, Blinkit, and Milkbasket.
Its products are also available on BigBasket, Amazon India, and Flipkart.
Henfruit uses traceability and testing to distinguish its products in India’s largely unorganised egg market.
The company says it conducts daily quality tests through its own lab and independent third-party labs, and publishes the results on its website.
The fundraise comes amid growing consumer interest in branded and quality-assured food products, with food safety and transparency gaining importance in the FMCG sector.

The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has also stepped up scrutiny of food brands over misleading advertisements, unsubstantiated product claims and labelling violations, issuing more than 150 notices to food companies in recent months.
The increased regulatory focus has put greater emphasis on quality checks, traceability and transparency across the food value chain.

Meanwhile, investor interest in India’s consumer brands has also picked up, with startups in the food and snacking segments raising capital to expand manufacturing capabilities and strengthen distribution.

Last month, healthy snacking startup Troovy raised ₹100 Cr ($10.5 Mn) in a Series B round led by Fireside Ventures to expand manufacturing capacity, invest in R&D and strengthen its quick commerce and offline distribution.
Before that, D2C nutrition and dietary supplements startup Ace Blend raised $9.9 Mn to fund clinical trials, strengthen its supply chain, invest in R&D and develop new nutrition formats.
Last year, Henfruit’s rival Eggoz raised $20 Mn in a Series C round led by Gaja Capital.
